positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.catalyst: Semiconductors are staging a broad buy-the-dip rebound on 7/9 after a ~15% PHLX washout: China signaling it may ease restrictions on importing advanced US chips, SK Hynix's US-listing ADR >7x oversubscribed, and UBS lifting Q3 DRAM contract-price forecasts +32% QoQ. Stock-specific: Goldman's James Schneider RAISED his AMD price target to $640 from $450 citing strong AI demand (~20% upside from entry). AMD +3.0% pre-market to $533.00 from $517.41 close; oil easing and yields well-behaved support the risk-on tape.
positions.driver: AMD is the cleanest non-chasing expression of today's chip rebound: a high-beta AI leader with its OWN fresh, specific catalyst (a +42% Goldman target raise to $640) layered on top of the sector-wide tailwind, off a deeply oversold base. Chose the 1x single name over SOXL (3x semi bull) deliberately — SOXL had already gapped +10.2% pre-market ($174.82→$192.61), past the 8-10% no-chase threshold, and 3x on an extended bounce-in-a-downtrend carries violent reversal risk. AMD at +3.0% is not chasing and the 1x vehicle bounds drawdown. Preferred over MU (+4.7%, more extended) and NVDA (+0.7%, muted move). Asymmetric: coordinated bullish catalysts into an oversold, sentiment-reset sector, with a hard 6% stop.
positions.risks: This is a bounce within this week's AI-valuation-fear downtrend — if the 'dot-com valuations / hawkish Fed / AI-capex-return doubts' narrative reasserts, semis can roll back over and a 1x long still gives back the gap. Single-name headline/China-policy risk (a reversal of the import-easing signal would hit AMD directly). Entered pre-market at +3.0%, so a fade to unchanged is a plausible near-term drawdown. Hard stop at $501.02 (-6%).
